subject: Workplace Skills
title: The Silent Brainstorm
description: A quick, practical guide to The Silent Brainstorm.

hook.text: Traditional brainstorming produces fewer ideas than having people write ideas independently first.

buildup.text: In group brainstorms, social pressure and anchoring bias suppress original thinking.

discovery.text: Brainwriting has everyone write ideas silently for five minutes, then share. Quantity jumps dramatically.

twist.text: Introverts often have the best ideas but never share them in verbal brainstorms. Writing levels the field.

climax.text: Try this: five minutes silent writing, then round-robin sharing. No idea is discussed until all are heard.

punchline.text: Write first, talk second. Better ideas surface.

quiz.question: Why does brainwriting produce more ideas than verbal brainstorming?
options: Writing is always faster than speaking
It removes social pressure and anchoring bias
People feel obligated to fill more paper
